facts.text: Rocheport was founded in 1825 by Joseph Kinney and quickly became a vital riverport for settlers and traders.
The town’s name means “rocky port” in French, reflecting its early role as a river trading hub.
Rocheport sits on the Missouri River and is home to the historic Rocheport Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The Katy Trail, a 225‑mile bike path built on a former railroad right‑of‑way, cuts through Rocheport’s middle, linking it to the rest of Missouri.
During the Civil War, Rocheport played a significant role in the state’s history, with local residents and organizations preserving its historic buildings.
Rocheport’s early days were shaped by Native American trade, as a Sauk, Meskwaki, and Ioway village near Moniteau Creek was noted by Zebulon Pike in 1806.
